D14·w5v1 — 2026-09-16
chose: 3.3 implementation rulings within D13, from building and dry-running it: (1) The transcript scan VOIDS a rep only on a hidden branch-tip sha (every `refs/heads` tip of the source repo other than the base commit) or an explicit `--hidden-term`; a hidden PATH in the transcript is a warning, never a void. (2) The comparator's RECORD is hidden separately: `--hide-record <slug,…>` removes `.sofar/initiatives/<slug>` from the cell before its one commit; nothing is hidden by default, the operator names it (for 3.4: `--hide-record r1-fixes`). (3) A fix that fails to build or pack is the arm's own failure and scores 0 in the mean; only voids, missing candidates without a build failure, missing eval runs, unequal parameters and an unstated loop cost withhold. (4) The fix cell keeps the repo's committed hooks and `.mcp.json`; they reach the runner's pinned sofar install, sandboxed by inheritance, so both arms work in the same developer environment; no candidate shim is written in fix mode.
over: Voiding on the branch NAME (`r1-fixes` appears legitimately in the cell's own record — self-improve notes cite it — and in absolute paths under file_touched events, so a name scan voids honest reps); hiding records by default (the evaluator would carry a list of initiative names it has no business knowing); withholding on an unbuildable fix (it would let a broken arm escape a loss).
because: The dry run on the fixture clone showed the record inside the cell already names the comparator's initiative and the source repo's paths, so only content the agent could not have seen without reaching the hidden history — a tip sha — is evidence of a leak. D13 §7 says a voided rep withholds; a fix that does not build is not a leak, it is a result the evaluator can see (build failed), and D9 §6's whole point is that the evaluator can see fail.
